the same for every row, set
from the class balance of the
For each row, p - y, where p =
Fit a small tree to these
Score of two rows as trees are added (illustrative)
row with an RLF ahead (y = 1): p rises
At 0 trees every row has the same starting p. Each tree then moves the score only a
little (learning rate 0.05), and is fitted to what the previous trees still get wrong.
a) Random subsample for each tree
Blue: used by this tree. Gray: left out.
leaf value = amount added to the score
All nodes of a level are split before the next one,
c) How a split and a leaf value are chosen (second-order boosting)
For each row, g = p - y (gradient) and h = p(1 - p) (hessian).
gain = G_L²/(H_L + λ) + G_R²/(H_R + λ) - G²/(H + λ)
G and H are the sums of g and h over the rows of the node (L = left child, R = right child).
leaf value = - G / (H + λ), with λ = 1 (L2 regularization, default).
No early stopping: all 300 trees are kept.
